answer: Each identity must complete a prescribed chain of sequential modular squarings, where each result depends on the previous one; a Wesolowski proof lets others verify the work efficiently. An attacker can run chains for multiple clones on separate hardware, but cannot divide one chain among GPUs to shorten its delay, so every additional identity demands another full computation and imposes a physical time and resource bottleneck. The vault may guard admission, while basalt and harbor mark distinct checkpoints, not shortcuts.
